newsitem.title: USA: NERC warns of power shortages in U.S. this summer.
newsitem.headline: NERC warns of power shortages in U.S. this summer.

text.p: The North American Electric Reliability Council (NERC) warned Monday that parts of the Midwest and New England could face power shortages this summer as air conditioners push the power grid to its limits.
NERC, in a report assessing summer power demand, pointed to the loss of several big nuclear power plants serving those regions as the main cause for concern.
"Electric utilities in parts of Illinois and Wisconsin will have difficulty serving expected customer needs during peak use periods this summer," NERC said in a statement summarizing the report.

The report said an estimated loss of 4,700 to 6,500 Megawatts (MW) of nuclear generating capacity and the limited ability to move power into the region on existing lines "is likely to result in electricity supply shortages."

"Although the utilities in these states have made extensive preparations to mitigate these problems, such shortages could require controlled interruption (rotating blackouts) of electric service to customers in portions of the region," NERC President Michael Gent said.

Most of the problems lie with nuclear power plants operated by Commonwealth Edison Co (ComEd), the Chicago-based utility and Unicom Corp subsidiary, which serves customers in Illinois and neighboring Wisconsin.
Of ComEd's total 11,852 MW nuclear generation capacity, 4,236 MW - about 36 percent - will remain shut into next year as the Zion and LaSalle plants undergo extensive overhauls.

NERC also warned of shortages in New England, where the long-term loss of about 3,400 MW of generation capacity at Northeast Utilities' Millstone nuclear units in Connecticut is expected to last through a second summer.
The three Millstone units were shut in early 1996 amid safety concerns.
Gent mentioned extensive measures taken by New England utilities, many already in place last year, to avoid outages.
"However, if the situation deteriorates, utilities in New England are prepared to disconnect electric service to customer facilities for short periods on a rotating basis."
Last summer was unusually mild in New England, a factor that dampened air conditioning demand and helped spare the region from rolling blackouts.

According to a Reuter survey of plant operators, outages at U.S. nuclear power plants last week totaled 30,929 MW, a 55 percent rise from a year ago and about 31 percent of the country's overall 99,657 MW nuclear power capacity.
Nuclear power typically accounts for about 12 percent of total U.S. power generation.
NERC, in its report summary, said other parts of the country were unlikely to face elctricity supply problems barring problems with their high-voltage transmission systems.
